# MenuFlyout

Headers: `winui/ui/menus/MenuFlyout.hpp`, `winui/ui/menus/MenuItem.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/menus/MenuFlyout.hpp`.

A list of commands in a popup: hung from an anchor element (a click on a [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor toggles it) or opened at a point with [show_at()](flyout.md#show_at) for a context menu.

The flyout sits in the tree in its anchor's place and owns the anchor ([set_anchor()](flyout.md#set_anchor)); the menu floats in the [Window](../tree/window.md)'s overlay layer, cascades into submenus, and closes on invoke, light dismiss or Escape. Placement and [show()](flyout.md#show)/hide() come from [FlyoutBase](flyout.md#class-flyoutbase). The declarative form is [ui::MenuFlyout](#uimenuflyout).

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto menu  = std::make_unique<ui::MenuFlyoutControl>();
ui::ButtonControl* options = menu->set_anchor(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Options"));
menu->set_items({
    {.text = "Open", .on_click = [&] { open_file(); }},
    ui::MenuItem::sub_item("Send to", {{.text = "Bluetooth"}, {.text = "Desktop"}}),
    ui::MenuItem::separator(),
    ui::MenuItem::toggle("Repeat", /*checked=*/true),
});
ui::MenuFlyoutControl* flyout = stack->add(std::move(menu)); // the stack owns flyout and anchor

// Also a context menu: a right-click on the anchor opens it at the pointer.
options->on_context_requested([flyout, options](std::optional<ui::Point> at) {
    flyout->show_at(at.value_or(options->bounds().center()));
});

// Or declaratively:
stack->add(ui::MenuFlyout{
    .items   = {{.text = "Reset"}, ui::MenuItem::separator(),
                ui::MenuItem::toggle("Repeat", true)},
    .anchor  = ui::Button{.text = "Options"},
}.build());
```

## `ui::MenuFlyout`

A list of commands in a popup, hung from an anchor. Builds a [ui::MenuFlyoutControl](#uimenuflyoutcontrol). A [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor opens it on click. To use it as a context menu, call `show_at(point)` on its [`.control`](#uimenuflyout-control) handle from an `on_context_requested` handler. The built element takes the anchor's place in the tree, and the menu floats in the window's popup layer.

Example: 
```cpp
bool repeat = true;
window.set_content(ui::MenuFlyout{
    .items   = { { .text = "Reset", .on_click = [&] { repeat = true; } },
                 ui::MenuItem::separator(),
                 ui::MenuItem::toggle("Repeat", true, [&](bool on) { repeat = on; }),
                 ui::MenuItem::sub_item("Sort by", {
                     ui::MenuItem::radio("Name", true),
                     ui::MenuItem::radio("Date") }) },
    .anchor    = ui::Button{ .text = "Options" },
});
```

```cpp
ui::MenuFlyout{
    .items, .is_open, .placement, .placement_alignment, .light_dismiss, .style, .margin,
    .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_opened, .on_closing,
    .on_closed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .anchor
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-items"></span>`items` | `ui::Binding<std::vector<ui::MenuItem>>` |  | The menu's entries: items, toggles, radio items, separators and submenus. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-is_open"></span>`is_open` | `ui::TwoWayField<bool>` | `{false}` | Whether the flyout is showing. Two-way with [ui::bind()](../core/namespace-ui.md#bind): closing it writes false, and a false that [`on_closing`](#uimenuflyout-on_closing) cancels is put back to true. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-placement"></span>`placement` | `ui::Binding<ui::PopupPlacement>` | `{ui::PopupPlacement::Below}` | Which side of the anchor it opens on, centered on the anchor; PopupPlacement::Below by default. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-placement_alignment"></span>`placement_alignment` | `ui::Binding<ui::PopupPlacementAlignment>` | `{ui::PopupPlacementAlignment::Center}` | How the menu lines up with the anchor along that side. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-light_dismiss"></span>`light_dismiss` | `ui::Binding<bool>` | `{true}` | Whether an outside click or Escape closes it; true by default. Off, it stays open until [`is_open`](#uimenuflyout-is_open) turns false, hide() runs or a command in it runs. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_opened"></span>`on_opened` | `ui::Action` |  | The flyout is showing. A two-way [`is_open`](#uimenuflyout-is_open) has been written by then. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_closing"></span>`on_closing` | `ui::Callback<ui::Decision(const ui::PopupClosingArgs&)>` |  | Gets why it is about to close; return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep it open. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_closed"></span>`on_closed` | `ui::Callback<void(ui::PopupCloseReason)>` |  | Gets why it closed, once the close fade has finished. A two-way [`is_open`](#uimenuflyout-is_open) has been written by then. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::MenuFlyout>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uimenuflyout-anchor"></span>`anchor` | `ui::Spec` |  | The in-tree element the menu hangs from. |

## `ui::MenuFlyoutControl`

Derives from `ui::FlyoutBase`.

A list of commands in a popup: hung from an anchor element (a click on a [Button](button.md#uibutton) anchor toggles it) or opened at a point with [show_at()](flyout.md#show_at) for a context menu.

The flyout sits in the tree in its anchor's place and owns the anchor ([set_anchor()](flyout.md#set_anchor)); the menu floats in the [Window](../tree/window.md)'s overlay layer, cascades into submenus, and closes on invoke, light dismiss or Escape. Placement and [show()](flyout.md#show)/hide() come from [FlyoutBase](flyout.md#class-flyoutbase). The declarative form is [ui::MenuFlyout](#uimenuflyout).

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto menu  = std::make_unique<ui::MenuFlyoutControl>();
ui::ButtonControl* options = menu->set_anchor(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Options"));
menu->set_items({

    ui::MenuItem::sub_item("Send to", {{.text = "Bluetooth"}, {.text = "Desktop"}}),
    ui::MenuItem::separator(),
    ui::MenuItem::toggle("Repeat", /*checked=*/true),

ui::MenuFlyoutControl* flyout = stack->add(std::move(menu)); // the stack owns flyout and anchor

// Also a context menu: a right-click on the anchor opens it at the pointer.

// Or declaratively:
```

### items

```cpp
const std::vector<MenuItem>& items() const
```

The items. Toggle and radio items' is_checked() track clicks made in the menu and the properties their `checked` is bound to.

### set_items

```cpp
void set_items(std::vector<MenuItem> items)
```

Replaces the items; an open menu closes first. The menu redraws when the command of any item changes, submenus included, and follows every bound `checked` while it holds the items.

### handle_global_shortcut

```cpp
bool handle_global_shortcut(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

The shortcut of an item, in the menu or in a submenu, invokes that item whether the menu is open or not.

### transition_opacity

```cpp
float transition_opacity() const override
```

The menu's opacity during its open and close transitions. A menu that slides in ([Theme::popup_motion](../themes/theme.md#popup_motion)) opens fully opaque, and one that fades in blends in. Closing fades it out over the theme's close duration.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Picks up the theme's menu open and close durations, then advances the flyout's transition.

## struct MenuItem

One entry of a menu. The plain case is `{.text = "Open", .on_click = [&] { open(); }}`; the factories below spell out the other kinds. The fields follow the spec order: what the item shows, then the command and the handlers, then the submenu.

[`on_click`](#on_click) is a copyable std::function, since items live in a std::vector built from a brace list, which only copies. A handler must not capture a move-only value.

Items are plain values: the menu that holds them ([MenuFlyout](#uimenuflyout), [MenuBar](menu-bar.md#uimenubar), a context menu, the window's system menu) keeps its own copy, so a toggle's or radio item's current state is read back from that owner's [items()](#items) with [is_checked()](#is_checked), or followed through [`on_checked_changed`](#on_checked_changed). [`text`](#text), [`icon`](#icon), [`shortcut`](#shortcut), [`enabled`](#enabled) and [`checked`](#checked) take a value or a property: bound to a property, every menu built from the item follows it, and a click writes a two-way [`checked`](#checked).

Radio items form a group in one of two ways. Bound with [`.checked = ui::selects(choice, value)`](#checked), the items bound to the same property are the group, wherever they sit in the menu. Unbound, a run of radio items next to each other in one list is a group, so a separator or any other item between two runs starts a new one.

Example: 
```cpp
enum class Size { Small, Large };
ui::Property<std::string> note;
ui::Property<bool>        word_wrap{true};
ui::Property<Size>        size{Size::Small};

std::vector<ui::MenuItem> items{
    {.text = "Copy", .icon = ui::Symbol::Copy, .shortcut = ui::Ctrl + ui::Key::C,
     .on_click = [&] { ui::clipboard().set_text(note.get()); }},
    ui::MenuItem::separator(),
    ui::MenuItem::toggle("Word wrap", ui::bind(word_wrap)),
    ui::MenuItem::radio("Small", ui::selects(size, Size::Small)),
    ui::MenuItem::radio("Large", ui::selects(size, Size::Large)),
    ui::MenuItem::sub_item("Send to", {{.text = "Desktop"}, {.text = "Mail recipient"}}),
    ui::MenuItem::split("Paste", [&] { note = ui::clipboard().text().value_or(""); }, {{.text = "Paste as text"}}),
};
auto flyout = std::make_unique<ui::MenuFlyoutControl>();
flyout->set_items(std::move(items)); // or a ui::MenuBarItem's items
```

### text

```cpp
Binding<std::string> text {}
```

The text. Falls back to the command's text.

### kind

```cpp
MenuItemKind kind = MenuItemKind::Item
```

Which kind of menu item this entry is; the factories below set it. Defaults to a plain Item.

### icon

```cpp
Binding<IconSource> icon {}
```

The icon, drawn 16x16. Falls back to the command's icon.

### shortcut

```cpp
Binding<KeyCombo> shortcut {}
```

The keyboard shortcut. It fires app-wide and invokes the item, and its text is shown in the shortcut column. Falls back to the command's.

### shortcut_text

```cpp
std::string shortcut_text {}
```

Shown instead of the shortcut's own text.

### enabled

```cpp
Binding<bool> enabled {true}
```

A disabled item is drawn dimmed, skipped by the keyboard, and its shortcut does not fire; a disabled command disables it too ([is_enabled()](#is_enabled)).

### checked

```cpp
Binding<bool> checked {false}
```

The checked state of a Toggle or Radio item. Two-way from a [`ui::Property<bool>`](../core/property.md) or [ui::selects()](../core/namespace-ui.md#selects): the item follows the property in every menu built from it, and a click writes the new state back before [`on_checked_changed`](#on_checked_changed) runs.

### command

```cpp
CommandRef command {}
```

The command, run after [`on_click`](#on_click) with [`command_parameter`](#command_parameter). The command also supplies the text, icon and shortcut the item does not set, and disables the item while it is disabled.

### command_parameter

```cpp
std::string command_parameter {}
```

Passed to the command's execute.

### on_click

```cpp
std::function<void()> on_click {}
```

Runs on a click, after the menu has closed, and after a toggle or radio item has changed.

### on_checked_changed

```cpp
std::function<void(bool checked)> on_checked_changed {}
```

Called when a Toggle or Radio item's [`checked`](#checked) changes through the menu (a click, a key, a shortcut, or a group-mate being checked), after a two-way [`checked`](#checked) has been written. A change of the bound property does not call it.

### items

```cpp
std::vector<MenuItem> items {}
```

The submenu of a SubItem or Split item.

### toggle

```cpp
static MenuItem toggle(std::string text, Binding<bool> checked = false, std::function<void(bool)> on_checked_changed = {})
```

A toggle item: a click flips [`checked`](#checked) (drawn as a check mark) and reports the new state to [`on_checked_changed`](#on_checked_changed) before [`on_click`](#on_click) runs.

### radio

```cpp
static MenuItem radio(std::string text, Binding<bool> checked = false, std::function<void(bool)> on_checked_changed = {})
```

A radio item: a click checks it and unchecks the rest of its group (see above); clicking a checked one leaves it checked. Each item unchecked this way writes false into its own two-way [`checked`](#checked).

### separator

```cpp
static MenuItem separator()
```

A 1px line between groups of items; never focused or invoked.

### sub_item

```cpp
static MenuItem sub_item(std::string text, std::vector<MenuItem> items)
```

A submenu item: invoking it (click, Right, Enter, Space, or a 400 ms hover) opens [`items`](#items) as a cascading submenu beside it. It has no [`on_click`](#on_click) of its own.

### split

```cpp
static MenuItem split(std::string text, std::function<void()> on_click, std::vector<MenuItem> items)
```

A split item: the item runs [`on_click`](#on_click), and the chevron button at its right edge opens [`items`](#items) as a submenu.

### from_command

```cpp
static MenuItem from_command(const Command& command, std::string parameter = {})
```

An item built entirely from [`command`](#command): its text, icon, shortcut and action.

### display_text

```cpp
std::string display_text() const
```

[`text`](#text), or the command's text when [`text`](#text) is empty.

### display_icon

```cpp
const IconSource& display_icon() const
```

[`icon`](#icon), or the command's icon when [`icon`](#icon) is empty (an empty [IconSource](../rendering/icon-source.md) when neither is set).

### display_shortcut

```cpp
KeyCombo display_shortcut() const
```

[`shortcut`](#shortcut), or the command's shortcut when it is empty.

### display_shortcut_text

```cpp
std::string display_shortcut_text() const
```

What the shortcut column shows: [`shortcut_text`](#shortcut_text) if set, else [display_shortcut()](#display_shortcut)'s "Ctrl+S" text (empty when there is no shortcut).

### is_checked

```cpp
bool is_checked() const
```

The check state: [`checked`](#checked)'s value. In a menu's [items()](#items) it is the current state, whether a click or the bound property set it last.

### is_enabled

```cpp
bool is_enabled() const
```

Enabled, and its command (if any) is too.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const
```

Can hold focus in a menu: not a separator, and enabled.

### has_submenu

```cpp
bool has_submenu() const
```

Opens a submenu (a SubItem, or a Split item with items).

## Enumerations

### MenuItemKind

```cpp
enum class MenuItemKind
```

Which kind of menu item a [MenuItem](#struct-menuitem) stands for.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Item` | a plain command |
| `Toggle` | a check item |
| `Radio` | one of a group of exclusive items |
| `Separator` | a line between groups |
| `SubItem` | `items` open as a submenu |
| `Split` | invokes like an Item, and `items` open from its chevron |
